app.description: Time tracking that adapts to how you work.
about.title: About
about.logo: The logo of EightPerDay, the number eight in a yellow circle
nav.label: Main areas
home.title: Time
login.title: Sign in
login.lead: With a passkey on this device, or with your name and password.
login.passkey.noscript: Passkeys need JavaScript. Use your password instead.
login.passkey.failed: The passkey did not sign you in. Try again or use your password.
login.throttled: Too many failed attempts. Please wait %d seconds.
login.expired: This step has expired. Please start again.
login.noaccount.title: No account yet
login.noaccount.text: Whoever runs the program makes a one-time link for the first account at the server's console with eightperday link --admin. It lasts one hour.
code.title: Code from your app
code.lead: Enter the six-digit code your authenticator app shows for EightPerDay.
code.label: Code
code.invalid: The code is wrong or was already used. Wait for the next one.
setup.title: Create your account
setup.lead: You were invited. Choose how you want to sign in.
setup.lead.admin: This is the first account. It administers the program.
setup.reset.title: New sign-in
setup.reset.lead: Choose a new way to sign in to the account %s. The old one stops working.
setup.username.hint: Small letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore.
setup.method: How do you want to sign in?
setup.method.passkey.hint: Your device unlocks with a fingerprint, face or PIN. Nothing to remember, nothing to steal.
setup.method.totp.hint: A password plus a six-digit code from an app on your phone.
setup.method.password.hint: Simple, but only as safe as the password.
setup.invalid.title: This link does not work
setup.invalid.text: The link is unknown, was already used, or has expired. Ask an administrator for a new one.
setup.error.name: This name is not allowed. Use small letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore.
setup.error.script: A passkey needs JavaScript. Choose a password instead.
setup.totp.title: Add the authenticator app
setup.totp.lead: Scan the code with your authenticator app, then enter the code it shows.
totp.qr.alt: QR code for the authenticator app
password.hint: At least %d characters. A sentence is easy to remember and hard to guess.
password.error.short: The password needs at least %d characters.
password.error.mismatch: The two passwords are not the same.
account.title: Account
account.passkeys.lead: Sign in with your device's fingerprint, face or PIN.
account.passkey.name: Name of the passkey
account.passkey.remove.confirm: This passkey will no longer sign you in.
account.password.has: You can sign in with a password.
account.password.none: You sign in without a password. You can set one.
account.password.remove.confirm: You will then sign in with a passkey only. The authenticator app goes too.
account.totp.on: Signing in with the password also asks for a code from your app.
account.totp.off: Add a code from an app on your phone to the password.
account.sessions.lead: Sign out here or on every other device.
account.error.lastmethod: This is your last way to sign in. Add another one first.
account.error.name: The display name must not be empty.
admin.title: Accounts
admin.invite.lead: There is no sign-up. An invitation is a one-time link you pass on yourself.
admin.invite.name.hint: Leave it empty to let the person choose.
admin.link.once: It is shown only now and works once, for %d days. Pass it on in a safe way.
admin.disable.confirm: The account can no longer sign in, and its sessions end. Its data stays.
admin.error.lastadmin: The program needs at least one active administrator.
licenses.title: Licenses
licenses.lead: EightPerDay is free software. These are the licenses of everything inside it.
error.notfound.title: Not found
error.notfound.text: There is nothing at this address.
error.internal.title: Something went wrong
error.internal.text: The server could not finish this. Please try again in a moment.
error.forbidden.title: Not allowed
error.gate.title: Not signed in
error.gate.text: The sign-in gate named an account that cannot be used here.
done.sessions: All other sessions are signed out.
home.managed: Managed by %s: the schedule and the pay come from there.
start.title: Who do you work for?
start.lead: Add an employer, a client or private work. Each has its own way of tracking; you can change it at any time without losing anything.
start.hours.hint: Optional. Makes a schedule for target and balance; it can be changed per weekday later.
mode.week_sum.hint: One number per week; the next week starts empty.
mode.schedule.hint: Hours per day against a target per weekday, with balance and overtime.
mode.plan.hint: The schedule counts as worked; you only book what differs and confirm the week.
mode.exact.hint: Start, end and breaks, with a stopwatch, split across projects.
mode.projects_only.hint: Time per project and week, no total working time.
absence.title: Absence
absence.health: Sickness is stored as a mark only, without a reason or a note.
absence.remove.confirm: The absence is removed; the history keeps it.
line.title: Quick entry
line.lead: For example 8-16:30 30m break · Fri -2h left early · Mon-Wed leave · 2h @Project #tag
track.error.title: That did not work
track.error.locked: This period is closed and cannot be changed.
track.error.conflict: Someone changed this in the meantime. Please reload and try again.
track.error.hours: Please give a duration such as 7:30, 7,5 or 7h30m.
track.error.clock: Please give start and end as times of day.
weeksum.title: Hours this week
weeksum.lead: One number for the whole week. The next week starts empty.
plan.title: The plan counts
plan.lead: Every day counts as in the schedule. Book only what differs, then confirm the week.
plan.exact.confirm: The planned days of this week become entries you can edit, and the employer switches to exact from this week on. Nothing is lost.
timer.title: Stopwatch
span.title: Add a span
entry.remove.confirm: The entry is removed; the history keeps it.
projects.title: Hours per project
projects.lead: This week, per project. There is no total working time in this mode.
employer.managed: %s sets the schedule and the pay. You book your times.
employer.name: Name
employer.mode.lead: How exactly you track. Switching keeps every entry; the calculation uses the mode valid on each day.
employer.mode.keeps: Data stays: earlier days keep their mode.
employer.schedule.lead: Target hours per weekday. A new schedule starts on its date and never changes the past.
employer.schedule.times: Start and end are optional; they are used when planned days become entries.
employer.pay.lead: With a valid-from date; each entry keeps the rate it was booked with.
employer.pay.unit.hint: Per assignment: day or job. Flat: week, month or year. Standby: per hour (–), per day with standby, or per job (call-out, active only).
employer.archive.confirm: The employer disappears from the lists. Its records stay and stay in your export.
employer.delete.confirm: This setting is removed. Entries keep their rate.
reports.title: Reports
reports.export.lead: Everything stored about you, with the correction history (JSON), or your entries as a table (CSV).
reports.hints.title: Working Hours Act
reports.hints.lead: Only you see this. Working time of all employers counts together (§ 2 Abs. 1 ArbZG). A note, not legal advice.
hint.day_over_10h: %s h in one day, more than 10 hours (§ 3 ArbZG)
hint.week_over_48h: %s h in one week, more than 48 hours (§ 3 ArbZG)
hint.rest_under_11h: only %s h of rest, less than 11 hours (§ 5 ArbZG)
orgs.title: Organizations
orgs.lead: An organization manages the time tracking of its members. It never sees your private employers.
orgs.none: You are not a member of an organization.
orgs.info.title: Your organization uses time tracking
orgs.info.what: What is stored: your working time with this organization, breaks, leave and absences, and corrections.
orgs.info.who: Who sees it: you, and the administrators of the organization.
orgs.info.why: What for: working time rules, pay and leave planning, not for rating performance.
orgs.info.private: Your private area stays untouched by the organization and cannot be read by its administrators.
orgs.info.supervisor: The organization has switched on the presence view: administrators see whether you are present or absent today, without reasons.
orgs.create.lead: You become its administrator. Members are added from the accounts of this program.
org.presence.lead: Only present or absent, without reasons and without history.
org.members.lead: Each member books on their own employer of this organization; you set the schedule and the pay.
org.end.confirm: The membership ends today. The records stay with the organization; the person keeps a copy in their export.
org.error.lastadmin: The organization needs at least one administrator.
org.add.hint: People without an account are invited in Accounts first.
org.templates.lead: New members start with one of these.
org.features.off: All off. They stay off unless you switch them on here.
org.features.agreement: Works agreement (date, version, scope) or why none is needed
org.features.agreement.placeholder: Works agreement time tracking of 2026-11-01, v1, all staff
org.features.needconfirm: Switching on needs the works agreement and your confirmation.
legal.activate.lead: With these features the organization processes personal data of its staff and is responsible for it. EightPerDay only provides the tool; it replaces neither a legal review nor a works agreement. Before switching on, clarify:
legal.activate.council: Is there a works council? Then a works agreement or its consent is in place (§ 87 BetrVG; in Austria §§ 96, 96a ArbVG).
legal.activate.informed: The staff were informed beforehand (Art. 13 GDPR).
legal.activate.documented: Purposes, roles, retention and reports are set and documented.
legal.activate.processor: With a hoster: a data processing agreement is in place (Art. 28 GDPR).
legal.supervisor: The presence view is an additional means of monitoring and usually subject to co-determination. Use it only with a works agreement and a documented purpose. Members see that it is on.
legal.title: Legal templates
legal.lead: Drafts for employers who use EightPerDay: a skeleton of a works agreement, an entry for the record of processing activities, and the kinds of data the program stores. The texts are in English, with the German terms.
legal.disclaimer.title: No legal advice, not checked by a lawyer
legal.disclaimer.text: These are drafts to start from, written from the software's side. Whoever uses the program as an employer is responsible for its lawful use and has the texts checked and adapted, together with the works council and the data protection officer where there are any.
legal.file.readme.lead: What the templates are, and what the software does to help.
legal.file.agreement.lead: A skeleton of a works agreement on time recording and leave with EightPerDay.
legal.file.record.lead: An entry for the record of processing activities (Art. 30 GDPR).
legal.inventory.lead: Every kind of record the program stores, with its purpose, whose it is and how it is deleted, generated from the code. The download lists every field with its purpose.
legal.footer: A tool, not legal advice. The organization is responsible for using it lawfully.
done.exact: This week is now recorded exactly.
weeksum.spread.hint: Spreads the total over the working days by the schedule (Monday to Friday without one). From this week on you enter hours per day.
weeksum.spread.confirm: Split the total of this week into days? From this week on you enter hours per day.
done.spread: The week is split into days.
absencepay.average: At the average of the weeks before
absencepay.method.hint: Public holidays and sickness usually at the planned hours, leave at the average of 13 weeks. Monthly salaries need no rule.
reminder.title: Leave left in %d
reminder.text: %s days of leave are still open; the year ends on %s, in %d days. Plan them in good time.
reminder.notice: Your employer pointed out on %s that leave not taken can lapse at the end of the year.
reminder.nonotice: Your employer has not recorded such a notice. Leave usually lapses only after one (BAG, 9 AZR 266/20). Information, not legal advice.
notice.title: Notice on lapsing leave
notice.lead: In Germany leave lapses at the end of the year only after the employer asked in time to take it and pointed out that it lapses otherwise (BAG, 9 AZR 266/20). Here that notice is recorded with its day.
notice.text: Wording or where it was given
notice.text.placeholder: Letter of 1 October: please take your remaining 5 days by 31 December, or they lapse.
notice.hint: Record the notice only once it was given to the person, in text form and for the leave still open. Information, not legal advice.
org.notices: Notices on lapsing leave still owed
org.notices.lead: Members with leave of this year still open, to whom the organization has not recorded the notice that it lapses. Without it the leave usually does not lapse. Opening this list goes into the members' access log.
org.notices.none: No notice owed: every member with open leave has one.
access.title: Access to your data
access.lead: Who of an organization read, changed or decided what of your data, and when. Your own work is not listed. A page of the organization opened several times on one day is listed once, with the first time.
access.intact: The log is complete and unchanged.
access.broken: Warning: the log was changed after it was written.
access.none: Nobody else has accessed your data.
approval.title: Approval
approval.lead: Your organization approves weeks and leave. What is handed in cannot change until it is decided.
approval.week.locked: This week is handed in or approved.
approval.submit.hint: After that the week cannot change, unless a correction is approved.
approval.withdraw.confirm: Take this back? You can hand it in again.
employer.daysplit.hint: Split at midnight, a night of 22:00 to 6:00 counts 2 hours for the first day and 6 for the next.
employer.absencepay.lead: Which absences are paid, and how. Without a rule an absence is unpaid.
employer.surcharges.lead: A percentage on top for night, Sunday, holiday or overtime minutes.
surcharge.window.hint: Only for night: the clock window, such as 20:00 to 6:00.
surcharge.base.hint: Only with a monthly salary; otherwise the hourly rate counts.
org.reviews.lead: Weeks and leave handed in by members. You never decide your own; a rejection needs a reason.
org.reviews.own: Your own request: another administrator of the organization decides it.
legal.approval: Members hand in weeks and leave; what is handed in is locked until an administrator decides. Every look at the data goes into the member's access log.
region.DE-BY-AUGSBURG: Bavaria: city of Augsburg (with the Peace Festival)
region.DE-BY-PROTESTANT: Bavaria: municipalities without Assumption Day (not mainly Catholic)
region.DE-SN-CATHOLIC: Saxony: municipalities with Corpus Christi (named in the ordinance)
region.DE-TH-CATHOLIC: Thuringia: municipalities with Corpus Christi (mainly Catholic)
list.title: List
list.codes: V leave · S sick · O day off · C time off in lieu · H public holiday · ½ half a day · AM/PM morning/afternoon · ? requested
correction.title: Correct the time account
correction.lead: A payout or a cap changes the balance from its day on, with its reason. The history of the days stays as it is.
correction.reason.example: Paid out with the November salary
list.approved.hint: The organization approved this week. A change goes to it as a request; until it decides, the approved values count.
list.error.reason: A change to an approved week says why.
done.requested: The change is requested. The approved values count until the organization decides.
leave.title: Leave
leave.adjustments: Including %s days carried over or corrected.
leave.lead: Mark the days off and book them as planned leave. Weekends and public holidays in between cost nothing.
leave.lead.approval: Mark the days off and ask for them: the request goes to the organization, which decides it.
day.title: Day
day.lead.typed: The hours typed in the list hold the bookings: what they leave is not booked on projects.
day.lead.projects: No hours typed in the list: the bookings make the day's hours.
report.week.title: Weekly report
report.week.heading: Weekly report, week %d
all.title: All employers
all.heading: All employers, week %d
all.hint: An employer shows only on the days it is active. Earnings from the pay rules and the incomes of each day.
day.incomes.lead: A job with its client, commission, photos, tips, and how it was taken.
day.error.details: Kilometres as a number (12,5), standby as hours (8 or 7:30).
employer.pay.salaries.hint: A monthly salary with 13th or 14th month pay, spread over the year.
employer.pay.half.hint: Per assignment per day: what a morning or an afternoon pays (4a or 4 PM in the list). Empty pays half the amount.
employer.standbywork.hint: For the time account. Active standby usually is working time, passive standby usually is not; this is no legal advice.
day.info.standby.counts: %s hours of standby count as working time.
day.request.title: Approved week
day.request.lead: Changes to the details and income of this day go to the organization as a change request, with a reason. The approved values count until it decides.
sheet.detail.hours.hint: One column of hours. Other employers and projects are summed into the day.
sheet.detail.projects.hint: The hours of the first employer and its projects side by side; other employers are summed into the day.
sheet.detail.employers.hint: A column per employer; its projects open next to it.
sheet.reason.title: Ask for a change
sheet.hint.codes: leave, sick, day off, half days
sheet.hint.sum: Empty next to projects: their sum
sheet.error.value: Not understood: %s. Hours such as 8, 8,5, 7:30 or 8-16:30 30m, a half day as 4v or 4n, a code U, K, F, ZA, ½U.
schedule.lead.sheet: Hours of a day are typed on the start page:
employer.key.hint: One to three letters a to z. In the journal, f3 books three hours on the employer with the key f. Empty: the first free letter of the name.
